text:
ada: Heads-up — ran a deep nsys + perfetto trace on the KV read/write hotspot that spikes under fused_attn_fast + flash_attn_v3. timeline + perfetto link below.

matt: nice, what machine? repro on H100 or A100?

ada: H100 dev node (4x H100). repro is a dynamic-batching workload with many short prompts + long context reuses (prefix caching on). batch window 8ms, max_batch 48.

sophia: ok, why do you think it's the KV path and not the attention kernel itself?

ada: timeline shows attention kernel completes quickly but immediately after there's a burst of small memcpy+kernel launches that saturate the L2 and cause the following requests to stall. NVTX regions: [ATTN_FORWARD] -> [KV_WRITE] -> [KV_READ] repeated. KV_READ kernels are serialized at stream-level.

liam: can you paste the nsys summary? even a small snippet helps

ada: pasted snippet from nsys summary:
```
CUDA Kernel: fused_attn_fast    time: 1.8ms  occ: 0.72  regs: 64
CUDA Kernel: flash_attn_v3     time: 1.1ms  occ: 0.55  regs: 92  (tile=64)
CUDA Kernel: kv_read_chunks    time: 2.4ms  occ: 0.12  memory_stall: high
Memcpy HtoD: 0.9ms  count: 12  small_chunks
Memcpy DtoH: 0.0ms  count: 0
```

sophia: kv_read_chunks occ 0.12 is alarming. looks like memory-bound low-parallelism work

ada: perfetto flame shows repeated short memcpy+kernel pairs on the same SMs. hypothesis: our KV write path uses a global mutex + single stream for all KV ops, forcing serialization and preventing overlap with compute.

matt: that would explain low occupancy. are we using pinned staging buffers for KV uploads?

ada: not consistently — old path used cudaMemcpy with default stream, plus we create a fresh cudastream per request which serializes because we call cudaEventSynchronize in several places. I'll try enabling a preallocated pinned pool + per-stream async copy.

perf-ci-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://perfetto.example/trace/abc123 (flamegraph, kernel timeline, memory ops)

liam: also curious about kernel selection heuristics — at seq_len ~800 we're picking fused_attn_fast which uses reg-heavy tiled kernels. flash_attn_v3 gets chosen for longer seqs but has heavier L2 use. maybe switch to flash_attn_v2 for mid-range lengths?

sophia: we should add a small rule: if seq_len in [512,1024] and batch_size < 8 prefer flash_attn_v2 (lower regs) else fused for big batches. Also avoid single-stream KV serialization — use stream pool + round-robin and record cuEvents for ordering.

ada: quick experiment: switched to pinned pool + cudaMemcpyAsync into per-request stream, removed explicit cudaEventSynchronize in KV write. result: kv_read_chunks time dropped from 2.4ms -> 0.7ms and overall tail latency (p95) improved by ~18% on the test harness.

matt: awesome. can you open a small PR with the pinned pool + stream pool and add a regression test that runs nsys capture on small harness (we can auto-accept perf-ci if no perf regression)?

ada: will do. next steps I noted in the trace thread:
- short-term: adopt pinned staging + stream pool, adjust cudaEvent usage
- medium: tweak kernel-selection heuristics for seq_len/batch combo
- long-term: consider KV sharding per-GPU L2 bank / reduce L2 conflicts, and instrument Warp occupancy per-kernel

liam: for the PR include the perfetto link and the before/after nsys command and summary. also add a flag so Dedicated customers can opt-in (safe default on)

sophia: also log nvtx region names from runtime so traces map to stages easily. small change but huge debugging ROI.

ada: agreed. I'll open the PR after I run the full 4x H100 harness tomorrow. thanks all :lock: :sparkles:

matt: :thumbsup: 

perf-ci-bot: note: reproduced trace on A100 rack? Not yet — please mark in PR if verified on A100 as well.
